short_term.title: Complete freeCodeCamp 'Programming with Google Go Specialization' fundamentals course
short_term.description: Go appears in 5/11 postings (45%) but is completely absent from your resume. A strong entry-level candidate should have at least basic Go competency. Complete the free Coursera 'Getting Started with Go' module and the 'Go with Tests' free tutorial to build working knowledge. This typically takes 40-60 hours of focused study; start with 5-10 hours on GolangBot's free tutorial to test compatibility with your learning style.

short_term.title: Build a small Go backend project (HTTP server + database) and publish on GitHub
short_term.description: Simply completing a course is not enough; Go adoption in the market is backend-infrastructure focused, and you need a concrete project demonstrating Go competency. Build a minimal HTTP REST API server using Go's net/http or a framework like Gin that connects to a database with basic CRUD operations. Publish to GitHub with clear documentation. This signals to hiring managers that you can apply Go to real systems, not just theory.

short_term.title: Study official React documentation (react.dev) Quick Start and build a small component library
short_term.description: React appears in 3/11 postings and you have JavaScript but no frontend framework specifics. Postings increasingly expect full-stack capability. Work through the official React Quick Start (free, interactive, ~2-3 hours) then build a reusable component library (form inputs, modals, etc.) demonstrating React hooks, state management, and testing. This is more valuable than a course certification for demonstrating practical capability.

medium_term.title: Complete System Design Primer GitHub repo and document 3 distributed system design case studies
medium_term.description: System design is increasingly expected at entry level (3/11 postings explicitly mention it; it's implicit in microservices roles). Work through the free System Design Primer focusing on foundational concepts: scalability, load balancing, caching, databases, message queues. Then document 3 case studies of systems you've built or analyzed. Publish these as a blog or GitHub wiki.

medium_term.title: Contribute to 1-2 open-source Go projects (e.g., Kubernetes, etcd, or other CNCF tools)
medium_term.description: Go is strongly represented in cloud-native tooling. Deepen your Go competency and demonstrate professional code review standards by contributing 2-3 meaningful PRs to established Go open-source projects in the CNCF ecosystem. This signals production-readiness and familiarity with industry-standard codebases. Start with issues labeled 'good first issue' in cloud-native projects. This builds both Go skills and open-source experience valued by Canonical, 1Password, Cohere, and Quora.

medium_term.title: Build a full-stack React + FastAPI microservice project and document the architecture
medium_term.description: Combine emerging gaps (React, REST APIs clarity, system design language). Build a full-stack project: a React frontend consuming a FastAPI backend microservice with proper REST API design patterns, authentication, error handling, and deployment documentation. Document the system design decisions (why microservices, how you'd scale, deployment patterns). This signals full-stack readiness and bridges the gap between frontend and backend infrastructure roles.

long_term.title: Learn Java fundamentals and build 1-2 enterprise backend projects
long_term.description: Java appears in 5/11 postings (45%) but is completely absent from your resume. For a junior developer, Java is typically needed only if targeting enterprise / financial services companies (BMO, RBC, Scotiabank, Stripe) or large tech companies with existing Java codebases. If your target is enterprise or scale-up tech, invest in Java competency via a structured course followed by 2 real projects. For pure startups or AI-focused companies, Java may not be necessary. Prioritize this based on your target companies.

summary: You are highly competitive for entry-level to mid-level roles in the current market. Your Python, cloud (Azure), DevOps (Kubernetes, CI/CD), and AI/ML skills directly match 60%+ of the analyzed postings and are genuinely rare at the junior level. Your legacy modernization and GenAI expertise (LangGraph, RAG) are clear differentiators. However, three gaps limit your reach: Go (missing entirely; 45% of postings), React (missing; 27% of postings), and Java (missing; 45% of postings). Additionally, while you clearly understand system design and REST APIs, your resume doesn't use this terminology explicitly, which costs you discoverability. Quick resume wording improvements will immediately boost your profile; short-term projects in Go and React will broaden your appeal across entry-level tech roles; long-term Java investment depends entirely on whether you're targeting enterprise finance or general tech roles. Your current trajectory places you well above average for your experience level.
